s7rs96: This week you review two classes: **diminutives and augmentatives** (_un cafecito, un problemón_) and the **quantifiers algo, nada, alguien, nadie**. The situation: in Comayagua, on the night before Good Friday, the neighbours on a street make a coloured sawdust carpet for the procession, and something or someone is always missing.
10g0jsq: The most general form is **-ito / -ita**: remove the final vowel and add the ending, with the same gender: _casa_ → **casita**, _perro_ → **perrito**, _abuela_ → **abuelita**.
em86p: If the word ends in **-e**, **-n** or **-r**, or is very short, it usually takes **-cito / -ecito**: _café_ → **cafecito**, _camión_ → **camioncito**, _flor_ → **florecita**, _pan_ → **panecito**. The exact form varies a little from country to country.
woh5ur: Watch the **spelling**, because the sound doesn't change: _poco_ → **poquito**, _amigo_ → **amiguito**, _taza_ → **tacita**, _luz_ → **lucecita**.
uqwdiu: _Poco_ → **poquito**: the _c_ changes to _qu_ to keep the sound.
pmo1kr: The diminutive keeps the **gender**: _el problema_ → **el problemita**.
1vzjkgi: The diminutive doesn't only express **size** (_una mesita_). It often expresses **affection**: _mi abuelita, un perrito precioso, pobrecito_.
k9pb9u: It is also used for **politeness**: it softens a request or a wait. _Espéreme **un momentito**_. _¿Le sirvo **un cafecito**?_ _Es **un ratito** nada más_.
1q9n6lb: Some words with a diminutive have a **life of their own** and don't mean "small": **el bolsillo** (on clothes), **la ventanilla** (at the bank, on the bus). And don't confuse **calentito** (pleasantly warm) with **calentísimo** (too hot, week 12).
109dluu: With strangers, a polite diminutive (_un momentito, un favorcito_) softens things a lot. But in a formal text or one written for work, use it sparingly.
1n488dv: The one on clothes is **el bolsillo**; _un bolsito_ is a small bag.
s0upm4: To exaggerate playfully, Spanish has **augmentatives**. The most common are **-ón / -ona** and **-azo / -aza**: _un problemón_ (a very big problem), _un fiestón_, _un perrazo_, _un exitazo_.
g4xn85: **-azo** sometimes means **a blow**: _un golpazo_, _un portazo_ (slamming the door). **-ucho / -ucha** is pejorative: something ugly or poor quality, _un cuartucho_, _un hotelucho_.
wkyn89: Watch out: some words in _-ón_ are already **something else**: **el cajón** (in a piece of furniture), **el sillón** (a comfortable seat), **el cucharón** (for serving soup). With many augmentatives in **-ón**, the word becomes **masculine**: _una silla_ → **un sillón**.
1hr9ynm: The augmentative of _silla_ is masculine: **el sillón**.
xik2ku: **-ucho** is negative: it doesn't go with _preciosa_.
ew3m2n: For **things** use **algo** (positive) and **nada** (negative). For **people** use **alguien** (positive) and **nadie** (negative). The four words **don't change** and the verb is **singular**: _Alguien **llamó**_, _Nadie **sabe**_.
zpjr7s: In open questions, the normal choice is **algo** and **alguien**: _¿Necesitas **algo**?_ _¿Vino **alguien**?_ In negative answers you get **nada** and **nadie**: _No, no necesito **nada**_. _No, no vino **nadie**_.
11m95fn: Useful combinations: _algo de comer, ¿algo más? — nada más, alguien más_.
1rzn9bu: Where no goes, and a alguien, a nadie
7pf7a0: **Nada** and **nadie** after the verb need **no** in front: _**No** vino **nadie**_, _**No** compré **nada**_. If **nadie** comes **before** the verb, you don't use _no_: _**Nadie** vino_. Both sentences mean the same.
1aop0rq: When **alguien** or **nadie** is the person receiving the action, it takes **a**: _Veo **a alguien** en la calle_, _No conozco **a nadie** aquí_. But **after hay** there is no _a_: _Hay alguien en la puerta_.
1k517n5: This week these two positions are enough. In the next class you'll extend the system with _nunca, tampoco, ni… ni_.
1f579tm: _Nadie_ after the verb needs **no** in front.

1i0ctm8: The endings **-ito, -ita, -cito** carry the stress on the **i**: _CA-sa_ → _ca-SI-ta_, _ca-FÉ_ → _ca-fe-CI-to_. The word's rhythm changes, even though the base doesn't.
1jfhttq: Augmentatives in **-ón** carry the stress at the **end**, which is why they have a written accent: _pro-BLE-ma_ → _pro-ble-MÓN_, _FIES-ta_ → _fies-TÓN_. In **-azo** the stress is on the **a**: _pe-RRA-zo_.

1rdxn2d: Accent on **-ón** in the singular (_sillón, problemón_), no accent in the plural (_sillones_). Changes: **poco → poquito, taza → tacita, amigo → amiguito**.

zesb53: In the evening I went out for a walk and didn't see anyone in the main streets. Where was everybody? Suddenly, on a block near the cathedral, I found the whole neighbourhood: children, grandparents and young people were working on the ground with stencils and coloured sawdust.
1bxty7l: I asked if anyone needed help and a lady gave me a bucket and a little stencil. "Put a tiny bit of water on it, sweetheart, so the sawdust doesn't blow away," she told me. Nobody talked about sleeping. At three in the morning there was a little problem: a huge dog ran right across the design. Nobody shouted; everybody laughed and fixed it in no time.
